title: Telemetry signal curator and on-call prioritization harness
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce noisy SLO/latency alerting and improve signal-to-noise for on-call by introducing a telemetry 'signal curator' layer and an on-call prioritization harness. The curator will normalize and score telemetry (traces, metrics, logs) into a single signal_quality_score and surface only high-confidence degradations to downstream alerting. The prioritization harness will compute a responder_score for each alert (customer-impact, recent flapping, route criticality, escalation-cost) to drive who is paged and with what urgency.

Scope:
- Add a preprocessing stage in the metrics/log pipeline to compute windowed latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) and compute short-window deltas and an adaptive baseline.
- Enrich incoming spans with route metadata (customer_tier, route_version, model_variant) via a tracing-hook sidecar so alerts can be attributed by customer impact.
- Implement signal_quality_score: combines freshness, sample_coverage, metric_consistency (cross-signal agreement) and anomaly_strength into a 0-100 score.
- Build responder_score: weights customer_impact, recent_escalations, maintenance_window, and predicted_resolution_cost to decide paging policy (silent, push, phone).
- Ship lightweight anomaly detector (robust z-score + short-term exponential smoothing) in the pipeline as default, with a toggle to enable experimental ML model in later cycles.
- Add dashboards: signal quality index heatmap, responder distribution, and curated SLO incidents feed.

Design trade-offs and constraints:
- Latency vs accuracy: scoring must be computed in-stream with <500ms added tail to metric aggregation to avoid inflating SLO windows. We will operate on 1s aggregated buckets for high-traffic routes and 5s for low-traffic.
- Sampling: to preserve cost, trace enrichment will use route-aware adaptive sampling (higher sampling for high-priority routes).
- Availability: new pipeline step is best-effort; when unavailable, fallback to legacy thresholds to avoid missing alerts.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Signal curator produces a signal_quality_score for >95% of candidate alerts within the pipeline.
- False-positive alert rate (measured against labeled historical incidents) drops by >=40% vs current baseline for latency SLO alerts.
- At least two on-call teams report improved prioritization in a 4-week pilot (survey + feedback).
- Dashboards for signal quality and responder_score live in Grafana and linked from Console by release obs-2026.03.
acceptance_criteria: signal_quality_score computed for >95% of alert candidates within pipeline latency SLO
historical false-positive rate for latency alerts reduced by >=40% on test dataset
responder_score drives different paging policy for >= 60% of alerts in pilot routes
Grafana dashboards (signal-quality, responder-histogram, curated-incident-feed) deployed and linked in Console
fallback path to legacy threshold alerts verified end-to-end

notes: Do not enable experimental ML detector in production without cross-team signoff; default to EWMA+z-score for first release.
Follow-up item: explore integrating KV-cache hit-rate as a signal for model-serving routes (separate ticket).
Alerting policy mapping: responder_score < 20 => silent log + customer_incident_ticket; 20-50 => push; >50 => phone + push
Consider future: integrate runbook snippets directly into the curated incident feed based on responder_score and route tags.
